answer: In an agent market trading pigments such as umber, each identity must lock 100 tokens for 30 days before it can submit one bid per hour. The contract counts bids against the bonded key, so a mirror account needs its own deposit; reusing a bond adds no capacity. A cipher may conceal who controls the keys, but 1,000 bidding identities still require 100,000 locked tokens, imposing a capital requirement and a month of forgone returns on the attacker.
